import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 923

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/923](https://www.erdosproblems.com/923)
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (1969), 27-35.
- [Ro77] Rödl, V., *On the chromatic number of subgraphs of a given graph*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1977), 370-371.
-/

namespace Erdos923

open SimpleGraph

/--
Is it true that, for every $k$, there is some $f(k)$ such that if $G$ has chromatic number
$\geq f(k)$ then $G$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number $\geq k$?

This is true, as shown by Rödl [Ro77].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos923.lean"]
theorem erdos_923 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) (n : ℕ),
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph V, k ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
    ∃ H ≤ G, n ≤ H.chromaticNumber ∧ H.CliqueFree 3 := by
  sorry

end Erdos923

reformulations.difference: The Lean quantifier order is ∀ V n, ∃ k, ∀ G, apparently allowing the threshold to depend on the vertex type. The source asks for a threshold depending only on the target chromatic number.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These are equivalent because V ranges over arbitrary, including infinite, types. Fix n>0. If no uniform threshold existed, choose for each j a graph G_j with chromatic number at least j and no qualifying triangle-free subgraph. Their disjoint union U has chromatic number above every finite threshold. Applying the Lean hypothesis on U's vertex type gives a triangle-free H≤U with χ(H)≥n. Each restriction of H to a component G_j must be (n−1)-colorable; combining those colorings colors H with n−1 colors, a contradiction. The n=0 case is immediate, and the converse implication is immediate. This equivalence was proved independently in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The declaration allows arbitrary vertex types and uses an ℕ∞-valued chromatic number, rather than restricting to the finite version identified in Erdős's original paper.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a positive finite threshold K, graph-coloring compactness implies that χ(G)≥K is witnessed by a finite induced subgraph. Raise the chosen threshold to at least 1 if necessary, apply the finite-graph statement to that witness, and extend the resulting subgraph to G. Conversely, the arbitrary-graph statement specializes to finite graphs. Comparisons with finite naturals are unaffected by representing all infinite chromatic numbers as ⊤. This does not assert the separate, open infinite-chromatic-number variant: the target n remains finite and H may depend on n. The finite/arbitrary equivalence was proved in Lean using Rado's selection lemma.

reformulations.difference: The witness H≤G is a spanning simple graph on the same vertex type, whereas the source permits an ordinary subgraph with fewer vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Extend any ordinary subgraph by making omitted vertices isolated. This preserves triangle-freeness and cannot decrease its chromatic number, so the required lower bound survives, including empty boundary cases. Conversely, every spanning subgraph is an ordinary subgraph. A pointwise equivalence between the displayed existential and an existential over G.Subgraph was proved in Lean.

review.notes: The sole declaration is faithful. The source's affirmative answer and PROVED (LEAN) status agree with answer(True), research solved, and the formal_proof attribute. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and proves the combined equivalence to a uniformly quantified finite-graph statement using only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Empty-vertex, n=0/1, small complete-graph, and infinite complete-graph checks passed. The cited proof targets Lean 4.29.1; a scratch-only compatibility port to the available 4.33.1 preserved all theorem statements and also passed the standard-axioms check. Although the full Rödl PDF was blocked, the original Erdős question, website statement, publisher abstract, and cited formal proof suffice to verify the declaration.
